strategies.title: Concentric 1-5-10 angular packing
strategies.plan: Replace the random Gaussian cloud with a deterministic three-layer circular construction: one point at the origin, five points on radius \(r=1/(2\cos(\pi/10))\) at angles \(\pi/10+2\pi k/5\), and ten points on the unit circle at angles \(2\pi j/10\). The inner pentagon is staggered halfway between neighboring outer decagon points, and the chosen radius makes every closest inner--outer pair have distance exactly \(r\), matching the center--inner distance. All points lie in the unit disk, while opposite outer-decagon points have distance 2, so \(d_{\max}=2\); the other same-ring spacings are larger than \(r\), hence \(d_{\min}=r\). An auxiliary variable formulation is applicable in general—fix diameter at 2 and maximize \(t\) subject to smooth squared-distance inequalities \(\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge t\)—but this explicit symmetric construction needs no runtime optimizer and always returns exactly 16 finite 2D points. The calculated raw metric is \(r^2/4=1/(16\cos^2(\pi/10))\approx0.06909830>0.00153547329022\), hence the predicted `combined_score` is \(0.06909830/(1/12.889266112)\approx0.89063>0.0197911238456\).

strategies.title: Deterministic multistart epigraph refinement
strategies.plan: Use the current concentric configuration as one seed, add deterministic triangular-lattice, perturbed-ring, and fixed-seed random seeds, and retain the best exact squared ratio after every iteration. Normalize every iterate to diameter 2, introduce the auxiliary variable \(t\) for the minimum squared pair distance, and optimize the smooth approximation of constraints \(t \leq \|p_i-p_j\|^2\) using soft-min pair repulsion together with soft-max diameter control; the pairwise derivatives are analytic. Finish the best candidate with deterministic coordinate-wise directional search against the exact nonsmooth ratio, accepting only strict improvements, while retaining the original coordinates as fallback. This is a local-exploitation route because each accepted final move directly increases the exact evaluator quantity without changing point count, dimension, determinism, or finite-coordinate validity. The expected-gain check is that the returned refined candidate is accepted only when its directly computed raw `min_max_ratio` exceeds 0.0690983005625, so its predicted `combined_score` is strictly greater than \(0.0690983005625/(1/12.889266112)=0.890626383837\).

strategies.title: Six-point triangular core replacement
strategies.plan: Replace the center-plus-staggered-pentagon subsystem while initially retaining the ten outer boundary points: initialize six interior points as a centered two-row triangular-lattice patch with coordinates proportional to \((-\tfrac12,0),(\tfrac12,0),(-1,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}),(0,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}),(1,\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}),(0,-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2})\), then scale and center the entire set to diameter 2. Apply the same deterministic pairwise epigraph refinement, but allow all sixteen points to move; this lets the outer decagon deform only where core-to-boundary bottlenecks require it. The mesoscopic change is meaningful because it replaces the fivefold central coordination and its compulsory center-to-ring bottleneck with a six-site triangular contact network. Use a strict exact-ratio acceptance test versus the incumbent and return the unchanged incumbent if this topological seed does not improve it, preserving all hard constraints. The expected-gain check is that an accepted replacement has raw `min_max_ratio` strictly above 0.0690983005625 and therefore predicted `combined_score` strictly above 0.890626383837.

strategies.title: Free-hull triangular-lattice structural search
strategies.plan: Explore a genuinely different global topology by starting from a \(4\times4\) triangular lattice, with rows shifted alternately by one half spacing, then centering and scaling it to diameter 2. Include reflected, rotated, and deterministically sheared variants of this lattice as starts, and run the analytic smooth epigraph optimization followed by exact directional polishing; do not preserve circular rings or prescribe a center point. This permits the optimizer to choose a noncircular convex hull and a variable number of hull vertices, escaping the concentric construction's fixed 10-hull/5-inner/1-center contact graph. At every iteration use only finite NumPy coordinates, recenter after motion, normalize by the actual maximum pair distance, and keep the best exact candidate plus the incumbent fallback. The expected-gain check is that only an exact-ratio improvement over raw `min_max_ratio` 0.0690983005625 is emitted, giving predicted `combined_score` strictly greater than 0.890626383837.

strategies.title: Analytic-Jacobian epigraph contact polish
strategies.plan: Replace the final nonsmooth “minimum squared distance” polish with a second smooth epigraph solve in variables \((x_1,\ldots,x_{16},t)\), maximizing \(t\) subject to \(||x_i-x_j||^2-t^2\ge0\) and \(4-||x_i-x_j||^2\ge0\) for every pair. Supply the exact dense Jacobian of both constraint families: each separation constraint has gradients \(2(x_i-x_j)\), \(-2(x_i-x_j)\), and \(-2t\), while each diameter constraint has the negated coordinate gradients. Start from each normalized triangular-lattice/shear solution, retain only the literal measured ratio after renormalizing its actual diameter to two, and keep the pre-polish candidate as a fallback. This removes the discontinuous active-pair switching in the existing final pass while preserving all 120 lower-distance and 120 upper-diameter hard constraints directly. The checkable acceptance mechanism is to return a polished point set only when its explicitly recomputed squared ratio is strictly larger than the saved candidate’s squared ratio; otherwise return the saved candidate. With the proposed target raw metric \(0.0775841700>0.0775841541474\), the predicted combined_score is \(0.0775841700/(1/12.889266112)=1.000003013\), strictly exceeding 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Alternating six-point patch reoptimization
strategies.plan: After obtaining the best full 16-point epigraph solution, identify the six points nearest the centroid and freeze the remaining ten points, including all currently diameter-attaining hull contacts. Re-solve the same epigraph problem only for those six movable point coordinates and \(t\), retaining inequalities for movable--movable, movable--fixed, and fixed--fixed pairs; then freeze the improved six-point patch and reoptimize the complementary ten-point subsystem once. Use the same analytic constraint derivatives and normalize by measured diameter after each alternating pass, accepting a pass only if the literal all-pairs squared ratio improves. This is a mesoscopic replacement rather than another global perturbation: it lets the interior contact network change without allowing numerical drift of the established diameter scaffold. All pairwise constraints remain present in every subsystem solve, so neither the minimum-distance nor diameter condition can be violated by the replacement. With an accepted alternating-patch raw metric of \(0.0775841650>0.0775841541474\), the predicted combined_score is \(0.0775841650/(1/12.889266112)=1.000002948\), strictly exceeding 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Row-topology and annular topology portfolio
strategies.plan: Add deterministic structurally distinct epigraph starts rather than only affine images of the four-by-four triangular patch: a staggered \(5\)-\(6\)-\(5\) three-row triangular patch, a staggered \(4\)-\(5\)-\(4\)-\(3\) four-row patch, and the explicit center-plus-pentagon-plus-decagon arrangement already present as the fallback. Normalize every start to diameter two, run the full smooth epigraph solve with exact constraint Jacobians, and compare literal recomputed squared ratios across all outcomes. The distinct row populations change both the candidate convex-hull cardinality and the interior/hull adjacency graph, so they can escape a local optimum whose active graph is inherited from the \(4\times4\) patch. Include the current triangular result as an unconditional fallback and accept a structural outcome only under a strict measured-ratio comparison, which preserves validity even if all new topologies converge poorly. With an accepted structural raw metric of \(0.0775841800>0.0775841541474\), the predicted combined_score is \(0.0775841800/(1/12.889266112)=1.000003142\), strictly exceeding 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Diametral-pair gauge multistart epigraph
strategies.plan: Fix one currently diametral pair at \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\), eliminating translation, rotation, scaling, and the numerically weak diameter normalization direction before optimization.  Optimize the remaining coordinates and an auxiliary separation variable \(t\) under the smooth inequalities \(\|p_i-p_j\|^2-t^2\ge0\) and \(4-\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge0\), with dense analytic derivatives for both constraint families.  Use deterministic, genuinely distinct starts: staggered \(4\times4\) lattice, square lattice, concentric 1–5–10 arrangement, a 3–5–4–4 triangular-row patch, and fixed-seed broad Gaussian configurations, each canonically aligned to its own diametral pair.  Retain the literal best squared ratio after recomputing all 120 distances, so every returned point array remains a valid 16-by-2 finite construction even if a solve fails.  Expected-gain check: acceptance requires the directly recomputed `min_max_ratio` to exceed 0.0775841541474, and the tighter gauge/analytic epigraph solve is predicted to reach `combined_score` 1.00001, strictly above 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Alternating hull-and-core subsystem replacement
strategies.plan: Starting from the best free-hull lattice solution, classify the convex-hull vertices with a monotone-chain hull computation and treat those vertices as the boundary subsystem and all other sites as the core subsystem.  Alternate two constrained epigraph solves: first hold the hull fixed while optimizing the core and \(t\), then hold the core fixed while optimizing the hull and \(t\); after each full cycle perform one unrestricted anchored epigraph solve to restore coupled contacts.  In every subsolve retain both lower pair-distance constraints and upper diameter constraints for all 120 pairs, not merely pairs internal to the moving subsystem, so moving a subsystem cannot silently break the global objective.  Use analytic derivatives restricted to the moving coordinate columns and accept a cycle only after literal full-matrix squared-ratio evaluation exceeds the saved incumbent.  This is a mesoscopic replacement mechanism because it permits the boundary contact graph to rearrange against a re-packed core rather than only perturbing all points simultaneously.  Expected-gain check: the implementation returns the saved configuration unless a full-distance check gives `min_max_ratio` \(>0.0775841541474\); a successful accepted alternating cycle is predicted to give `combined_score` 1.000006, strictly above 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Row-topology contact-graph exploration
strategies.plan: Explore several noncongruent triangular-row seeds rather than transformations of one 4-by-4 patch: use rows of lengths \(3,5,5,3\), \(4,5,4,3\), \(3,4,5,4\), and \(2,4,4,4,2\), with alternating half-unit horizontal offsets and vertical spacing \(\sqrt3/2\).  Normalize each seed to diameter two, choose and fix a diametral pair as an anchored gauge, then run the same analytic-\(t\) epigraph problem; this lets the optimizer change both hull cardinality and the interior Delaunay/contact graph.  Include the existing staggered \(4\times4\) seed and incumbent as mandatory fallbacks, and compare every post-solve candidate using the exact squared evaluator rather than the solver’s \(t\).  The hard constraints are preserved during solving by the all-pairs lower and upper squared-distance inequalities, and normalization is applied only before exact candidate comparison.  This structural route can escape the current four-row lattice basin by changing which rows supply the diametral endpoints and which contacts support the free hull.  Expected-gain check: only a literal `min_max_ratio` greater than 0.0775841541474 replaces the fallback, and the best new row-contact basin is predicted to give `combined_score` 1.00002, strictly above 1.00000280888.

strategies.title: Contact-topology portfolio with analytic epigraph solve
strategies.plan: Replace the mostly symmetry-equivalent transformed lattice starts with a deterministic portfolio of genuinely different 16-point contact topologies: staggered triangular row counts `(4,4,4,4)`, `(3,4,5,4)`, `(3,5,5,3)`, `(4,5,4,3)`, the existing `1-5-10` construction, a `4-12` two-ring construction, and a golden-angle disk seed. For every seed, normalize its literal diameter to two and maximize an epigraph variable `t` subject to the smooth inequalities `||p_i-p_j||^2-t^2 >= 0` and `4-||p_i-p_j||^2 >= 0` for every pair. Supply the exact dense Jacobian of those inequalities to SLSQP, avoiding finite-difference noise at the dense active contact graph and allowing materially more useful starts within the former runtime budget. Include the old concentric arrangement as a hard fallback, recompute the literal squared ratio after normalization, and return a new result only when its measured ratio is strictly larger. The acceptance mechanism preserves all pairwise diameter constraints before normalization and strictly raises the same evaluator quantity whenever accepted; predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Delaunay-star mesoscopic replacement
strategies.plan: Starting from the best full solve, compute its Delaunay triangulation and choose the interior vertex with maximum Delaunay degree, breaking ties by smallest squared radius from the centroid. Hold every point outside that vertex's closed Delaunay star fixed, while jointly reoptimize the selected center and all of its Delaunay neighbors together with an epigraph separation variable; all 120 pair constraints remain present, so fixed-to-moving distances and the global diameter are hard constraints rather than penalties. Repeat once for the next two nonoverlapping stars selected from the original triangulation, then perform one global epigraph solve initialized from the patched arrangement. This provides a mesoscopic escape mechanism because a locally overconstrained triangular patch can change its contact graph without requiring the hull to move simultaneously. Normalize only by a similarity after each accepted patch and retain the pre-patch point set unless the recomputed literal squared ratio increases. The strict measured acceptance test preserves the incumbent fallback and gives predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Active-contact KKT polishing
strategies.plan: Take the strongest candidate and identify its active lower-distance pairs and active diameter pairs using a relative tolerance of `2e-7` after diameter-two normalization. Solve a constrained local epigraph problem retaining every original pair inequality, but add equality constraints for the currently active contacts and fix a rigid-motion gauge by setting one point at the origin and the y-coordinate of a second point to zero. Use analytic gradients for pair squared distances, then remove any equality whose Lagrange multiplier is negative or whose constraint becomes inactive, and repeat up to three deterministic active-set updates. This is distinct from another global restart: it directly removes the residual numerical slack that typically remains because SLSQP terminates on a nonsmooth contact change. Reject any polish whose recomputed all-pairs squared ratio is not strictly larger than the input, so neither the diameter nor the actual evaluator minimum can regress. The literal acceptance comparison is a checkable strict improvement mechanism with fallback; predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Deterministic disk-code atlas multistart
strategies.plan: Replace the redundant rigid-motion starts with a deterministic atlas of genuinely different normalized configurations: staggered triangular patches with several aspect ratios, centered square/hexagonal patches, Fibonacci-disc samples, and concentric ring allocations \(1\!-\!5\!-\!10\), \(3\!-\!6\!-\!7\), and \(4\!-\!5\!-\!7\).  For every atlas member, introduce the separation epigraph variable \(t\), maximize \(t\), and impose the smooth inequalities \(\|p_i-p_j\|^2-t^2\ge0\) and \(4-\|p_i-p_j\|^2\ge0\), supplying the dense analytic Jacobian.  This explores basins with different hull cardinalities and radial layering rather than merely rotated copies of one triangular patch.  Normalize every accepted result to literal diameter two, score using the evaluator’s squared ratio, and retain the best point set together with the current explicit concentric construction as a fallback.  Hard validity is preserved because normalization only rescales all distances uniformly and each optimization candidate is evaluated after exact diameter normalization.  Expected-gain check: acceptance requires a directly computed squared ratio strictly above the retained incumbent ratio, otherwise the valid incumbent fallback is returned; an accepted atlas basin therefore has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Diametral-lens block replacement
strategies.plan: Starting from the best atlas result, identify all pairs within a small tolerance of the diameter and choose one deterministic diametral pair, then partition the remaining points by whether they lie closer to the first endpoint, the second endpoint, or in the perpendicular central lens.  Hold two blocks fixed while optimizing the third block plus epigraph variable \(t\) against all 120 lower-distance and upper-diameter inequalities; cycle through endpoint-side block, central-lens block, and the union of both side blocks.  After each block pass, run one anchored all-point epigraph solve with one diametral endpoint fixed, so translation null directions cannot degrade SLSQP conditioning.  This is a mesoscopic replacement mechanism: it permits coordinated relocation of several nearby sites and can change local contact graphs without requiring a full random restart.  Keep only literal post-normalization improvements in squared ratio, with the untouched input retained on every failed or non-improving subsystem solve.  Expected-gain check: each committed block replacement is checked against the same squared `min_max_ratio` and is accepted only when it strictly increases it, with fallback preserving the incumbent; any accepted replacement has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.

strategies.title: Barrier-central-path contact refinement
strategies.plan: Use the best feasible configuration from the structural and block stages and perform a deterministic interior refinement of the epigraph formulation, maximizing \(t\) plus a small logarithmic barrier over positive lower-separation and upper-diameter slacks.  Begin from a slightly contracted copy of the diameter-two configuration so all upper-bound slacks are strictly positive, use decreasing fixed barrier weights, then finish with a standard analytic-Jacobian epigraph SLSQP solve.  The barrier prevents early commitment to an arbitrary subset of tied nearest pairs and lets contact forces redistribute before the final nonsmooth boundary optimum is reached.  At every stage, normalize and compare the literal squared ratio, retaining only improvements; the original feasible configuration remains the fallback if a barrier iterate is nonfinite or loses score.  The hard upper bound is restored exactly by the final diameter normalization, while uniform scaling leaves the ratio unchanged.  Expected-gain check: the final candidate is committed only after its directly measured squared ratio strictly exceeds the saved one, otherwise fallback is used; an accepted central-path refinement has predicted `combined_score > 1.00000280888`.
